public_rationale: On January 1, 2025, under 'High confidence', Marcus predicted that AI agents would be endlessly hyped throughout 2025 but far from reliable, except possibly in very narrow use cases. OpenAI's CEO promoted agents in January and June 2025, saying they may 'join the workforce' and that agents could do real cognitive work. An independent benchmark revised in September 2025 found the best agent completed 30% of realistic workplace tasks on its own, with harder long-horizon tasks beyond reach.
limitations: The promotion shown comes from one company's CEO. It does not measure how much agents were promoted across the industry.
The benchmark simulates one kind of workplace. The latest test shown is from September 2025, not the end of the year.
Whether an agent use counts as a 'very narrow use case' is not defined by the speaker.

criteria.support_condition: Leading AI companies promoted agents as transformative during 2025, and independent tests published in 2025 show general-purpose agents failing a large share of realistic multi-step work tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Independent tests published in 2025 show general-purpose agents completing most realistic multi-step work tasks across broad uses, or agents were not prominently promoted in 2025.
